doc: How many octaves frequency * lacunarity^k (k = 0, 1, ...) start strictly below max_frequency, at least 1: 20 rows (frequency, max_frequency, lacunarity). Covers frequency above and equal to the maximum (n = 0 raised to 1), one octave, many (35 for 1 .. 1e6 at lacunarity 1.5, 59 for 1e-9 .. 1e9), lacunarity 1.1 to 1000, and the exact boundary with lacunarity 2.0 (3 * 2^3 = 24 is NOT below 24, so n = 3; 24.000001 gives 4; both exact in float64). No other row is within 1e-9 of a boundary (checked at build time): see octaves_below.fragile. The function loops forever for frequency <= 0 or lacunarity <= 1 with frequency < max, so they are not cases. Every row passes lacunarity explicitly; the Python default (2.03, what the callers use) is pinned by octaves_below.defaults. Integer output: exact.
